title: Ambient internal Hom from a locally closed finite-projective generator
statement: Let k be a field, let ell be prime and invertible in k, and let E be a finite extension of Q_ell with A = O_E/varpi^n, n >= 1 [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let X be a separated finite-type k-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], hence Noetherian. Let a:S -> X be a locally closed immersion and L a locally constant A-module sheaf with finite projective geometric stalks, in the precise intrinsic sense FlatModelProEtaleLisseProjective of [det-sf-flat-model-generation]. Use its canonical extension a_!L = g_*j_!L, with j open in the scheme-theoretic image and g closed, placed in degree zero. If M is an ambient derived A_X-module with bounded constructible cohomology [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], then the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] RHom(a_!L,M) has bounded constructible cohomology. All sites are small pro-etale [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the coefficient ring sheaves are constant, and no finite-Tor hypothesis on M is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, p. 57, calculation on a locally closed finite-projective generator; Lemmas 6.7.11 and 6.7.2 for exceptional restriction and direct image. Lean split of steps 1-7 and 9 of lem-per-finite-tor-internal-hom-any-field.

proof.text: The coefficient facts [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] make $A=R/\varpi^n$ a finite commutative ring. It is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finitely many elements. Moreover $\ell\in\mathfrak m_R$ because its extended absolute value is $\ell^{-1}<1$. Write $\ell=u\varpi^e$ by clause (5) of the first node; $e\geq1$, since $u$ is a unit and $\ell$ is in the maximal ideal. Thus $\ell^n=0$ in $A$. The integer $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$, as required for finite-coefficient direct-image finiteness. For a scalar $A$-module, finite as a set and finitely presented are equivalent: a finite module has a finite free surjection whose kernel is finite and hence finitely generated; a finite presentation has finite underlying cokernel.

source.place: Section 6.7, coefficient conventions; elementary specialization to R/varpi^n.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes every finite-type $k$-scheme below Noetherian. Such a scheme is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Its open subschemes are Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Each immersion is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2); its source is quasi-compact and its target quasi-separated, so it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), hence finite type. Composing finite-type morphisms is checked on affine charts by adjoining both finite sets of algebra generators. Consequently all locally closed strata, their scheme-theoretic closures, and the open complements used below are finite type over $k$ and Noetherian. The same permanence node makes morphisms between them qcqs. These are the geometric hypotheses needed below, without an assumption on the perfection or cohomological dimension of $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, reduction to constructible immersions: finiteness hypotheses for the strata.

proof.text: For such a scheme $T$, write $\mathcal B(T)$ for the ambient $A_T$-complexes with bounded cohomology and a finite constructible locally closed stratification for every cohomology sheaf, with finite locally constant module values. Step 1 identifies finite values with finitely presented values. Thus [lem-sfb-noetherian-global-constructibility] identifies this global convention with the affine-local convention in [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre]. The latter supplies zero, kernels, cokernels and extensions in the sheaf category. Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to conclude that $\mathcal B(T)$ is closed under isomorphisms, shifts and distinguished triangles. It is also closed under retracts: if $C\xrightarrow{s}D\xrightarrow{r}C$ has $rs=1$, then $H^q(C)$ is isomorphic to $\ker(1-H^q(s)H^q(r))$ on $H^q(D)$. Kernel closure gives constructibility, and the retraction gives vanishing whenever $H^q(D)=0$. This verifies precisely the thick closure required for the generation argument.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, triangulated closure; Lemma 6.3.9, idempotent-complete devissage.

proof.text: Ordinary inverse image $v^*$ for a morphism of these schemes preserves $\mathcal B$. With constant coefficients the pulled-back ring is the same constant ring, so the underlying functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^q(v^*C)=v^*H^q(C)$, preserving the cohomological interval. Pull back a witnessing partition by actual fibre products of its locally closed subschemes. For a stratum $\iota:Z\to T$ with base change $\iota':Z'=Z\times_TT'\to T'$ and $v':Z'\to Z$, one has $\iota'^*v^*\cong v'^*\iota^*$, since $v\iota'=\iota v'$ and inverse images are left adjoints of the strictly composing direct images. By [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] applied to $v'$, the base-changed trivializing covers trivialize $v'^*\iota^*H^q(C)$ with the identical finite module models. These strata are again a finite disjoint constructible locally closed partition, and the constant local modules are unchanged. Hence its cohomology remains constructible with finite values. This applies in particular to open and closed inverse images. The actual stratification pullback is [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. For constructibility of its subsets use [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-preimage]: every open in the Noetherian source is retrocompact, since its intersection with a quasi-compact open is again an open of a Noetherian space and hence quasi-compact. Thus its inverse-image hypothesis holds.

source.place: Lemmas 6.5.8 and 6.7.11, ordinary pullback used in the support triangle.

proof.text:
Ordinary pro-etale $Rf_*$ preserves $\mathcal B$ for every finite-type morphism $f:T\to V$ between these schemes. Choose a bounded constructible etale origin $C_0$ for $C\in\mathcal B(T)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Step 1 gives an annihilating integer $\ell^n$ invertible in $k$, so [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] gives $Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}C_0\in D^b_c(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Since $f$ is qcqs by step 2 and $C_0$ is bounded below, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives
$$Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}C\cong\nu_V^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}C_0.$$
The first cited node preserves cohomological intervals and identifies bounded constructible etale origin with intrinsic bounded constructibility, so this belongs to $\mathcal B(V)$. This invokes a sheaf-valued direct-image theorem, with no bound on the absolute Galois cohomological dimension of $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 and its use of Lemma 5.4.3 and Theorem 6.7.1; finite coefficients.

proof.text:
For a closed immersion $g:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with open complement $h:W\hookrightarrow T$, and $N\in\mathcal B(T)$, use [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle]:
$$g_*Rg^!N\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow Rh_*h^*N\longrightarrow g_*Rg^!N[1].$$
Its hypotheses are exactly that $T$ is Noetherian and $A$ finite. By steps 4 and 5, $Rh_*h^*N\in\mathcal B(T)$; step 3 and the triangle put $g_*Rg^!N$ there too. The complementary open is quasi-compact by step 2. The exactness of $g_*$ and the identity $g^*g_*\cong1$ are stated in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Apply the exact, constructible-preserving $g^*$ of step 4 to obtain $Rg^!N\in\mathcal B(Z)$. No constructible-preservation conclusion was assumed in the ambient support-triangle node.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.11, closed-support proof by the localization triangle.

proof.text:
Let $L$ be a locally constant sheaf with finite projective $A$-values on a stratum $S$, and $N\in\mathcal B(S)$. Then $L$ is site-perfect in degree zero, and [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,N)\cong L^\vee\otimes^L_{A_S}N.$$
Here $L^\vee$ is also a locally constant finite projective sheaf in degree zero: on a trivializing cover its value is $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$ for the finite projective scalar value $P$ of $L$. Explicitly write $P$ as the image of an idempotent $e$ on $A^r$; its dual is the image of the transposed idempotent on $A^r$. Tensoring with it is a direct summand of $r$ copies of the identity and is exact. Thus the displayed complex has $H^q=L^\vee\otimes H^q(N)$ and vanishes outside the same interval as $N$, independently of $r$. To see constructibility, use the finite stratification witnessing constructibility of $H^q(N)$, then restrict $L^\vee$ and refine its local trivializing cover with that of $H^q(N)$. The resulting module value is $P^\vee\otimes_A Q$, a finite module. Restriction of the displayed derived Hom to these site covers is justified by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Hence the original finite stratification witnesses constructibility of each cohomology sheaf, so $R\mathcal Hom(L,N)\in\mathcal B(S)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, local perfect-value Hom calculation; Stacks 08JJ and 08JB for the formal ringed-site statements.

proof.text:
Factor the given immersion a as j followed by g, with j open in its scheme-theoretic image and g closed. For the canonical object g_*j_!L from [det-sf-flat-model-generation], apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] separately to $g$ and to $j$, in exactly this order. Its pro-etale hypothesis is Noetherianity, established in step 2. For the closed case take its open factor to be the identity; for the open case take its closed factor to be the identity, so the exceptional inverse image is ordinary $j^*$. Since $g_*$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], the resulting formulas are
$$\begin{aligned}
R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(g_*j_!L,M)&\cong Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_Z}(j_!L,Rg^!M)\\
&\cong Rg_*Rj_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,j^*Rg^!M).
\end{aligned}$$
These are ambient internal sheaf Hom identities, without preservation hypotheses. Step 6 gives $Rg^!M\in\mathcal B(Z)$, step 4 gives $j^*Rg^!M\in\mathcal B(S)$, and step 7 puts the innermost Hom in $\mathcal B(S)$. Step 5 applied first to $j$ and then $g$ puts the whole expression in $\mathcal B(X)$. The factorization has not been interchanged, so no extra factorization-comparison assertion is needed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, internal adjunction for each locally closed generator, using Lemmas 6.7.11 and 6.7.2.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.7.13, with the localization proof of Lemma 6.7.11 and the finite-coefficient form of Lemma 6.7.2; perfect-on-strata generation as in Lemma 6.3.9.

theorem locallyClosedProjective_internalHom_constructible_anyField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : IsUnit (l : k))
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsNoetherian X]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (a : S ⟶ X) (ha : IsImmersion a)
    (L : proEtaleRingModules S (proEtaleConstantRing S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n)))
    (_hL : FlatModelProEtaleLisseProjective S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n) L)
    (M : proEtaleDerivedCategory X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n))
    (_hM : intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E n hn X M) :
    intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E n hn X
      ((derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u} (ProEt.topology X)
        (proEtaleConstantRing X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n))).obj
          (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            ((@flatModelProEtaleExtension S X inferInstance
              (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n) inferInstance
              (Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing l E n hn) a ha).obj L)), M))
